rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fabrication against God is belief in idolatry: gods have divinity and intercession, and world management returns to them.
rows.anchor: المراد بافتراء الكذب على الله الاعتقاد باصول الوثنية كالوهية الآلهة وشفاعتها ورجوع تدبير العالم إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning of punishment follows from the prohibition: association with God brings annihilation for shirk; the indefinite punishment signals its severity.
rows.anchor: وتنكير العذاب للدلالة على شدته وعظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure is despair at not attaining the hoped-for outcome; the statement is framed as a general principle because false causes cannot produce true, lasting good.
rows.anchor: الخيبة اليأس من بلوغ النتيجة المأمولة وقد وضعت الجملة في الكلام وضع الأصل الكلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse applies failure to fabrication in general, broader than the warning that those who fabricate against God do not prosper.
rows.anchor: لإثباتها الخيبة في مطلق الإفتراء بخلاف الآية الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points back to his discussion of the false blood on Joseph's shirt as another case showing that lies do not prosper.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم كلام في أن الكذب لا يفلح في ذيل قوله وجاؤا على قميصه بدم كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanaazuʿ is close in meaning to disagreement and derives from pulling something from its place; it takes a direct object or may govern bi-fi.
rows.anchor: التنازع قريب المعنى من الاختلاف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najwa means private speech; its original verbal-noun sense is speaking confidentially.
rows.anchor: والنجوى الكلام الذي يسار به، وأصله مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muthla is the feminine of amthal, meaning nearest or most fitting.
rows.anchor: والمثلى مؤنث أمثل كفضلي وأفضل وهو الأقرب الأشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “ideal way” is the customary idolatrous order governing Egypt, especially worship of the gods with Pharaoh foremost as the Copts’ deity.
rows.anchor: والطريقة المثلى السنة التي هي أقرب من الحق أو من امنيتهم وهي سنة الوثنية التي كانت مصر اليوم تدار بها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines ijmaʿ as collecting something after thought and deliberation.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكره الراغب - جمع الشيء عن فكر وترو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saff is arranging things in a straight line, such as people or trees; the word can function as a verbal noun or a result noun.
rows.anchor: والصف جعل الأشياء على خط مستو كالإنسان والأشجار ونحو ذلك ويستعمل مصدرا واسم مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may use saff as a verbal noun or mean “standing in ranks”; the command is to approach united and in agreement.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون بمعنى صافين أي ائتوه باتحاد واتفاق من دون أن تختلفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are urged to abandon division, marshal every stratagem, and meet Moses as one force so they can prevail.
rows.anchor: فتضعفوا وكونوا كيد واحدة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute follows Moses’ preceding admonition, which affected some of them because it was a clear statement of truth: they lacked proof for their gods’ divinity or intercession.
rows.anchor: ومن شأنها ذلك إذ ليست إلا كلمة حق ما فيها مغمض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute seems first to have arisen among the magicians; the call to form ranks suggests some were hesitant or intended not to confront Moses.
rows.anchor: أن الاختلاف إنما ظهر أول ما ظهر بين السحرة ومنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his officials saw the people’s disagreement as humiliating, whispered privately, and ignored Moses’ wisdom and admonition.
rows.anchor: أسروهم النجوى ولم يكلموهم فيما ألقاه إليهم موسى من الحكمة والموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They shifted to accusing Moses of sorcery and alleging a political plan to expel the Egyptians from their land.
rows.anchor: عدلوا عن ذلك إلى ما اتهمه فرعون بالسحر وطرح خطة سياسية لاخراج أمة القبط من أرضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expulsion charge portrayed loss of homes and property and a fall from prosperity into misery, while the Israelites’ oppression was visible to them.
rows.anchor: ففيه خروج من ديارهم وأموالهم وسقوط من أوج سعادتهم إلى حضيض الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh added that abandoning the contest would destroy their inherited idolatrous national way of life, a custom bound up with their collective identity.
rows.anchor: وأضافوا إلى ذلك أمرا آخر أمر من الجلاء والخروج من الديار والأموال وهو ذهاب طريقتهم المثلى وسنتهم القومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal exploits popular reverence for familiar national customs, which people often treat as sacred and heaven-given.
rows.anchor: والعامة تقدس السنن القومية وخاصة ما اعتادت عليها وأذعنت بأنها سنن ظاهرة سماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This was political incitement, not a defense of true religion: Moses’ proof had exposed idolatry’s falsehood, but the regime presented it as the basis of its power and survival.
rows.anchor: بل بعنوان أنها سنة ملية مقدسة تعتمد عليها مليتهم وتستند إليها شوكتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their tactic was to unite, keep their customary order, and attack as one force, since division and Moses’ victory would mean their destruction.
rows.anchor: فالرأي هو أن يجمعوا كل كيد لهم ثم يدعوا الاختلاف ويأتوا صفا حتى يستعلوا وقد أفلح اليوم من استعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh reinforced the call for unity with attractive promises, as another passage shows.
rows.anchor: وشفع ذلك فرعون بمواعد جميلة وعدهم إياها كما يظهر من قوله تعالى في موضع آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh treats earthly life as the only human life, containing all happiness and misery; the magicians instead affirm an everlasting life beyond it.
rows.anchor: وهو يرى أن ليس للإنسان إلا الحياة التي فيها وفيها سعادته وشقاؤه فإنهم يرون الأمر بالعكس من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the afterlife is eternal and earthly life is fleeting, they will not fear worldly loss if they gain there; this answers Pharaoh’s threat of death.
rows.anchor: إذا ربحوا في الحياة الأخرى الخالدة، وذلك قولهم لفرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The clear signs” alludes to several signs they witnessed: the staff became a serpent, swallowed the ropes and staffs, then returned to its former state.
rows.anchor: تلويح إلى أنهم عدوا ما شاهدوه من أمر العصا آيات عديدة كصيرورتها ثعبانا وتلقفها الحبال والعصي ورجوعها ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible alternative takes min as partitive: they saw one sign and believed God had many others; the author considers this reading far-fetched.
rows.anchor: آمنوا بأن لله آيات أخرى كثيرة ولا يخلو من بعد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khataya is the plural of khatiʾa and is close in meaning to sayyiʾa, a misdeed.
rows.anchor: الخطايا جمع خطيئة وهي قريبة معنى من السيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about coerced magic is coordinated with “our sins,” and min al-sihr explains what they were compelled to do.
rows.anchor: معطوف على { خطايانا } و { من السحر } بيان له والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words show coercion, either when they were summoned from their districts to Pharaoh or when the dispute and whispering led them into the contest.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنهم أكرهوا عليه إما حين حشروا إلى فرعون من خلال ديارهم وإما حين تنازعوا أمرهم بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request for forgiveness explains their refusal to prefer Pharaoh: they chose the God who created them and believe in Him to forgive their sins and coerced magic.
rows.anchor: أي إنما اخترنا الله الذي فطرنا عليك وآمنا به ليغفر لنا خطايانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s goodness and permanence explain why they prefer His forgiveness over Pharaoh’s favor; absolutely, nothing is better or more enduring than He is.
rows.anchor: أي خير من كل خير وأبقى من كل باق - لمكان الإطلاق -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their closing words deliberately answer Pharaoh’s claim that he can inflict the harshest and most lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الذيل نوع مقابلة لما في ذيل كلام فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first call God the one who created them because creation makes Him the source of every real good; compared with Him, all else is an illusion, grounding their choice over Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: لأن كونه تعالى فاطرا لنا أي مخرجا لنا عن كتم العدم إلى الوجود ويتبعه انتهاء كل خير حقيقي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Him their Lord fits their confession of faith and worship, since lordship includes ownership and governance.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني فلأن فيه إخبارا عن الإيمان به وأمس صفاته تعالى بالإيمان والعبودية صفة ربوبيته المتضمنة لمعنى الملك والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They use the name Allah because goodness rests on perfection, and God possesses every perfection, making Him absolutely good.
rows.anchor: لأن ملاك خيرية الشيء الكمال وعنده تعالى جميع صفات الكمال القاضية بخيريته المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their three descriptions carry the argument: they will not prefer Pharaoh because God created them, believe in Him because He is Lord, and hold Him best because He is God.
rows.anchor: لن نؤثرك على الذي فطرنا لأنه فطرنا، وإنا آمنا بربنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about Gehenna explains why they make forgiveness the goal of faith: one whose sins are not forgiven remains a criminal.
rows.anchor: تعليل لجعل غفران الخطايا غاية للإيمان بالله أي لأن من لم يغفر خطاياه كان مجرما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike worldly punishment, the criminal in Hell cannot escape torment through death, yet has none of the good or hope that makes life pleasant.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيها حتى ينجو من مقاساة ألم عذابها لكن منتهى عذاب الدنيا الموت

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines a daraja as a station conceived as upward ascent, unlike a darka, a station downward; hence paradise has degrees and Hell levels.
rows.anchor: الدرجة - على ما ذكره الراغب - هي المنزلة لكن يعتبر فيها الصعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakki means growing through sound growth: living with true belief and righteous action.
rows.anchor: والتزكي هو التنمي بالنماء الصالح والمراد به أن يعيش الإنسان باعتقاد حق وعمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses contrast the consequences of faith and good works with the criminal’s fate, answering Pharaoh’s threat and promise of reward and closeness.
rows.anchor: والآيات الثلاث الواصفة لتبعة الإجرام والإيمان ناظرة إلى وعيد فرعون ووعده لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eternal gardens are the reward for faith and righteous conduct, answering Pharaoh’s promise of payment; the high ranks answer his promise to make them close to him.
rows.anchor: قابلوا ذلك بأن من يأته مؤمنا قد عمل الصالحات فأولئك - وفي الإشارة البعيدة تفخيم شأنهم - لهم الدرجات العلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israʾ means traveling by night, and “My servants” refers to the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: الإسراء السير بالليل والمراد بعبادي بنو إسرائيل

words: فَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًۭا فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ يَبَسًۭا
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported reading takes the command as striking the sea with the staff; “a path” is the object by an extended, metaphorical attribution, originally striking the sea to make a path.
rows.anchor: وإن { طريقا } مفعول به لاضرب على الاتساع وهو مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verb can mean building or setting up, as in pitching a tent or laying a foundation.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد بالضرب البناء والإقامة من باب ضربت الخيمة وضربت القاعدة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib defines yabs as a place where water was and then disappeared; dark means the consequence of a thing.
rows.anchor: واليبس - على ما ذكره الراغب - المكان الذي كان فيه ماء ثم ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling what overwhelmed Pharaoh’s people an indefinite relative “what” and making the drowning its clause heightens the terror of the scene.
rows.anchor: وفي نسبة الغشيان إلى ما الموصولة المبهمة وجعله صلة لها أيضا من تمثيل هول الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Pharaoh did not guide his people refutes his claim that he showed them the path of right guidance; it is not redundant after saying he led them astray.
rows.anchor: وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In Nahj al-Balagha, Ali says Moses feared neither for himself nor simply the contest, but feared the dominance of ignorant people and regimes of error; al-Tabataba'i says this matches his earlier explanation.
rows.anchor: في نهج البلاغة قال عليه السلام لم يوجس موسى خيفة على نفسه أشفق من غلبة الجهال ودول الضلال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Jundub al-Bajali reports the Prophet saying to kill a sorcerer when caught, then citing the verse as meaning the sorcerer is safe nowhere; al-Tabataba'i says this application is unclear in context.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي

words: لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here taqwa means refraining from hostility and stubborn resistance out of fear of possible harm; dhikr means awakening to the truth, possibly believing it, paralleling fear with remembrance.
rows.anchor: يستأنس منه أن المراد بالإتقاء ها هنا هو التحرز من المعاداة واللجاج الذي هو لازم الخشية باحتمال الضرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glorification best follows the resurrection and judgment discussion: God’s absolute kingship includes guiding people by messengers and books, raising them, and judging their deeds.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الأنسب نظرا إلى انسلاك الجميع في سلك واحد وهو أنه تعالى ملك يتصرف في ملكه بهداية الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead close the entire preceding account of Moses and its consequences with glorification and awe.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يتفرع على جميع ما تقدم من قصة موسى وما فرع عليها إلى هنا ويكون بمنزلة ختم ذلك بالتسبيح والاستعظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context concerns receiving Quranic revelation: the Prophet is told not to rush his recitation before the angel has completed the revelation.
rows.anchor: السياق يشهد بأن في الكلام تعرضا لتلقي النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وحي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse pairs the command not to hasten with the supplication for more knowledge, placing the Prophet’s continuing learning beside his recitation.
rows.anchor: وحيه وقل رب زدني علما } السياق يشهد بأن في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command parallels the instruction not to move the tongue hastily; the Quranic passage says God gathers and recites it, then tells the Prophet to follow the recitation.
rows.anchor: لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports reports of a single, complete descent of the Quran in addition to its gradual descent: otherwise the Prophet could not hurry to recite what had not yet been revealed.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية مما يؤيد ما ورد من الروايات أن للقرآن نزولا دفعة واحدة غير نزوله نجوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says not to recite or dictate Quran to companions before its meanings become clear; the author finds no support for this in the wording.
rows.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن لفظ الآية لا تعلق له بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the verse as forbidding a request for revelation before God completes it; the author likewise finds this reading incompatible with the wording.
rows.anchor: وهو كسابقه غير منطبق على لفظ الآية

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses “the best of them in way” as the most knowledgeable and upright, saying that they had remained only a day.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { إذ يقول أمثلهم طريقة } قال أعلمهم وأصلحهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Majmaʿ reports an anonymous account: a man from Thaqif asked the Prophet what would happen to the mountains at resurrection; God would make them like sand and winds scatter them.
rows.anchor: قيل إن رجلا من ثقيف سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن جريح
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur, through Ibn al-Mundhir from Ibn Jurayj, gives a variant occasion: Quraysh asked Muhammad about the mountains, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى في الدر المنثور عن ابن المنذر عن ابن جريح ولفظه قالت قريش يا محمد كيف يفعل ربك بهذه الجبال

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses amt as elevation and ʿawaj as rough ground and raised mounds.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا } قال الأمت الارتفاع، والعوج الحزون والذكوات

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the caller whom people follow as a caller from God.
rows.anchor: وفيه في قوله تعالى { يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له } قال مناد من عند الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says people will stand barefoot and naked at the gathering, overwhelmed by sweat and labored breathing for fifty years; this explains the verse’s hushed voices.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبي عن الحسن بن محبوب عن أبي محمد الوابشي عن أبي الورد عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال إذا كان يوم القيامة جمع الله الناس في صعيد واحد حفاة عراة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Kafi, Abu Qurra claims God granted vision to Muhammad and speech to Moses; al-Rida argues Muhammad conveyed that God is unseen, incomprehensible, and unlike creation, so reports contradicting Quran and Muslim consensus are rejected.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الحسن عليه السلام فمن المبلغ عن الله إلى الثقلين من الجن والإنس { لا تدركه الأبصار }

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi says the Prophet would hasten to recite revelation before an ayah finished descending; the command told him to wait until its recitation was complete and ask for more knowledge.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولا تعجل بالقرآن } الآية، قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi’s version says the Prophet hurried for fear of forgetting; al-Tabataba'i rejects this because forgetting revelation conflicts with prophetic infallibility.
rows.anchor: عن السدي إلا أن فيه أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يفعل ذلك خوفا من النسيان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that after a husband struck his wife and the Prophet ordered retaliation, this verse was revealed before 4:34; the author says neither verse fits the event.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال لطم رجل امرأته فجلاءت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم تطلب قصاصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact Adam story recounts the couple’s expulsion after Satan’s whisper and chiefly explains the institution of religion and the reward for guidance or punishment for turning away.
rows.anchor: بيان قصة دخول آدم وزوجة الجنة وخروجهما منها بوسوسة من الشيطان وقضائه تعالى عند ذلك بتشريع الدين وسعادة من اتبع الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its mention of Adam’s repentance also connects the account to the earlier promise of forgiveness to those who repent, believe, and act righteously.
rows.anchor: ذكرها توبة آدم بقوله فيما تقدم { وإني لغفار لمن تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا ثم اهتدى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story depicts human earthly nature: God created people excellently, surrounded them with blessings, and placed them in a balanced garden, warning against excess and attachment to worldly desire.
rows.anchor: فقد خلقه الله سبحانه في أحسن تقويم وغمره في نعمه التي لا تحصى وأسكنه جنة الاعتدال ومنعه عن تعديه بالخروج إلى جانب الإسراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan tempts people to forget God and imagine that attachment to the world grants mastery over causes and lasting pleasure; worldly means fail, suffering compounds, and the person loses the garden of blessing.
rows.anchor: الذي يزين له الدنيا ويصور له ويخيل إليه أنه لو تعلق بها ونسي ربه اكتسب بذلك سلطانا على الأسباب الكونية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s episode preceded the legislation of religion; his garden was a barzakhic, non-worldly life, and the tree prohibition was advisory, so its violation brought an inevitable consequence rather than a legal punishment.
rows.anchor: إلا أن واقعته عليه السلام كانت قبل تشريع أصل الدين وجنته جنة برزخية ممثلة في عيشة غير دنيوية فكان النهي لذلك إرشاديا لا مولويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant here is a charge or admonition; the word is also used for edicts and codes.
rows.anchor: المراد بالعهد الوصية وبهذا المعنى يطلق على الفرامين والدساتير العهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisyan means forgetting and may also stand for abandoning something, since forgetting entails leaving it.
rows.anchor: والنسيان معروف وربما يكنى به عن الترك لأنه لازمه إذ الشيء إذا نسي ترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm means a firm intention or resolve toward something.
rows.anchor: والعزم القصد الجازم إلى الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm can also mean patience: patience is hard for the soul and requires a firmer, more settled resolve.
rows.anchor: وربما أطلق على الصبر ولعله لكون الصبر أمرا شاقا على النفوس فيحتاج إلى قصد أرسخ وأثبت

words: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means God charged Adam earlier, but he abandoned the charge and lacked firm resolve or patience to preserve it; the charge was the ban on eating from the tree.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى وأقسم لقد وصينا آدم من قبل فترك الوصية ولم نجد له قصدا جازما إلى حفظها أو صبرا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about commanding the angels is joined to an implied “remember”: remember the covenant and the time the angels were ordered to bow, showing Adam’s failure to keep the charge.
rows.anchor: معطوف على مقدر والتقدير اذكر عهدنا واذكر وقتا أمرنا الملائكة بالسجود له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He refused” answers the implied question about what Iblis did.
rows.anchor: وقوله { أبى } جواب سؤال مقدر تقديره ماذا فعل إبليس؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s warning follows Iblis’s refusal to bow and counsels Adam for his own good; “this enemy” refers to Iblis.
rows.anchor: تفريع على إباء إبليس عن السجدة أي فلما أبى قلنا إرشادا لآدم إلى ما فيه صلاح أمره ونصحا إن هذا الأبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to let Iblis expel them indirectly means not to obey him or become careless about his scheme, lest he gain power to expel and make them suffer.
rows.anchor: توجيه نهي إبليس عن إخراجهما من الجنة إلى آدم كناية عن نهيه عن طاعته أو عن الغفلة عن كيده

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi gives several explanations for Satan’s enmity, but al-Tabataba'i dismisses them as specious and not worth recounting.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الإمام الرازي في تفسيره وجوها لسبب عداوة إبليس لآدم وزوجه وهي وجوه سخيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true reason for Satan’s enmity is his expulsion from divine proximity, his banishment, and the curse laid on him until resurrection, as his own words show.
rows.anchor: والحق أن السبب فيها هو طرده من حضرة القرب ورجمه وجعل اللعن عليه إلى يوم القيامة
